verdict: Two major faults: the Java world import cannot work on a dedicated server (the server saves before WorldOpenReady), and /bmh rule does not check the player's level, which made HOOKS.md wrong and forced /bmh point to operators. The state rules hold: no lock is held across a game call, no unwrap on world, file or message data, and rules, config and choice live in files that survive a restart.

findings.what: On a dedicated server the import of a Java world's BMH rules always finds nothing. The dedicated open saves the world before it fires WorldOpenReady, and that save rewrites game_rules.dat with the vanilla keys only. The world is not new, so every rule comes back ON and the file bmh/rules.txt makes that permanent. A server owner who had set a rule to false in the Java mod gets it silently switched on.

findings.fix: Read game_rules.dat before the first save. `native_server_about_to_start` fires before load_world (dedicated.rs:1025), so the world folder may not be set there; `native_level_load` of minecraft:overworld fires while the world loads, before WorldOpenReady. Check that it comes before dedicated.rs:1253 and that `native_world_dir()` answers there, read the file then, keep the result in a SERVER_ static and let open_world use it. Add a dedicated server case to the game checks.

findings.what: on_perform_command ignores the player's level. Horizon checks one level for the whole /bmh root, the lowest of all its usages, so /bmh rule is safe only while every other /bmh usage is level 2 or more. HOOKS.md tells the other areas the opposite (each usage keeps its own level). Because of this the amulet area had to put /bmh point at level 2, so a player who is not an operator cannot use the point command that Java gives to every player.

findings.fix: In on_perform_command, after the line is known to be `bmh rule`, refuse when `player.permission < logic::COMMAND_LEVEL` (answer vanilla's unknown or no-permission text and set ran). Correct HOOKS.md "The /bmh command root" and log step 3. Then the amulet area can put /bmh point back at level 0.

findings.what: On a dedicated server, `/bmh rule` typed on the console, through RCON or through horizon-server answers "Unknown command". Console lines go to `native_perform_console_command`, which BMH does not hook. Java's `/gamerule bmh:...` works from the console, so an admin with no operator in the game cannot change a world rule.

evidence.ours: horizon/native/mixins/bmh/hook_perform_command.rs:2 "fn bmh_hook_perform_command(" (the only command hook; horizon-mixin.toml has no perform_console_command injection)
evidence.host: crates/horizon-client/src/game/dedicated.rs:2043 "if !self.perform_native_console_command(line.trim()) {"; native_server.rs:1525 "self.native_perform_console_command(line, &mut ran);" and :1528 "Text::translate(\"command.unknown.command\", &[])"; native_hooks.rs:4592 "A command a mod registered, typed on the dedicated server's console"
evidence.java: common/src/main/java/github/mrornithorynque/bmh/utilities/BMHGameRules.java (the rules are vanilla game rules, so the console's /gamerule reaches them)

findings.fix: Add a `perform_console_command` injection whose helper calls a settings function that runs the same `parse_rule_command` branch (no level check: the console is level 4, `native_feedback` answers on the console). List it in HOOKS.md.
